correctness.rationale: The proof defines the entire unrestricted conductance feasible class and full budget, invokes established convexity of each resistance to average over the price-preserving wreath-product automorphism group, and computes exactly two positive Laplacian eigenspaces (m antisymmetric eigenvalues 2x+(2m-2)y, m-1 pair-constant eigenvalues 2my). Hence matched resistance equals 2/lambda_a and nonmatched equals 1/lambda_a+1/lambda_b. The active worst-pair switches at t=x/y=1. Both scalar derivatives and their boundary signs are explicitly checked, yielding the three cases, the r=2 degeneracy and the exact optimum; averaging plus uniqueness of orbit solutions gives the two unrestricted support implications. The t=0 support remains connected for m>=2. The packaged checker reports 2497 exact/numerical assertions including rational full-matrix inverses and symbolic identities; random tests do not substitute for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Minimizing the maximum pairwise effective resistance is an independently motivated robustness design objective for adversarial terminal placement. The theorem identifies a positive-length interval where all optimal orbit weights stay identical despite differing link prices, a universal cost ratio two at which a full matching becomes dispensable, and an explicit first-order critical-window response. It is an exact natural classification and sharp support boundary on an infinite graph family; these facts are not routine consequences of knowing the graph spectrum or the generic SDP formulation.
